DSH COMPOSITE IDENTITY — issue #226 task 8.8 parts (a)–(c): the LAST targeted repair before the operator rules on debt. Branch slice-dsh-composite-b at HEAD 81d7fe87; adopt every commit.

WHERE THIS STANDS. The resolver port (417354ec, 25b40967 and their narrowings) is clean: the last council compared the cursor walk against glibc 2.42 execvpe.c and established NO high finding and NO specification defect. Its fresh validation ran all seven crate suites sequentially — 2,193 passed, zero failed — with fmt, clippy -D warnings, OpenSpec 15/15 and both bundle compiles green. Run 124cca78 then parked REVIEW-REFORGE-EXHAUSTED-MEDIUM because four MEDIUM findings survived two reforges, two of them security-flagged. The operator ruled: ONE more run scoped to exactly those four. If your council still finds mediums in the pnpm reader after your fixes, the operator rules on tracked debt — do not chase beyond R1–R4, and do not widen scope.

THE FOUR, verbatim from the chief of run 124cca78:

R1 MEDIUM security, author adversarial (panel R1): composite.rs:853,892-893 passes the flow-map value after consuming only one separator space to a scalar reader that checks its first character. Fresh built-doctor reproduction: engines: {node:  *missing}, {node:  &} and {node:  %bad} retain the valid control's composite f742ba0ece3e4684adf8398132b688a2ca70d6397b1f29fcef7e2b3ea15eb80d although the independent YAML parser rejects them. One-space *missing is refused; valid one-space and padded numeric controls both parse and preserve the composite. Separator padding must not hide a scalar's opening syntax. Producer and built-doctor refusal/control regressions and removal/restoration evidence are needed.

R2 MEDIUM correctness, author adversarial (panel R2): composite.rs:2943-2944 canonicalizes the selected invocation, selected_from at 1761-1771 exports that target as the executable, and doctor.rs:268 probes it. Fresh native executions of dsh -> /usr/bin/env, using both a searched name and absolute alias, exit 1 with the uutils executable-name mismatch and no stdout; doctor instead reports successful uu_env availability after executing the canonical target. Direct /usr/bin/env is the passing control. Preserve invocation semantics separately from canonical identity, or refuse an unestablished invocation before probing; cover both alias forms and the control with removal/restoration evidence.

R3 MEDIUM security, author security (panel S1): composite.rs:942-962 admits an implicit ignored block-mapping key without YAML's lookahead bound. Fresh built-doctor reproduction with peerDependencies and a 1,025-character ASCII key retains the same control composite although the independent parser rejects it; the 1,024-character control is valid. Enforce the implicit-key syntax boundary, including separation before the colon, without imposing a blanket line/value cap. Source: [YAML 1.2.2 section 8.2.2](https://yaml.org/spec/1.2.2/#822-block-mappings). Boundary/doctor regressions and removal/restoration evidence are needed.

R4 MEDIUM correctness/spec compliance, author spec-compliance (panel F1): composite.rs:3298-3300 admits an established env interpreter with no nonblank program argument; composite/tests.rs:4719 explicitly expects admission. Fresh native and built-doctor executions of both bare and blank-argument #!/usr/bin/env launchers failed to terminate and required the reproduction's external process-group timeout. The env sh control completed normally. The kernel supplies the launcher pathname as env's program, causing self-execution. AS1 requires cause-bearing pre-probe refusal for unestablished semantics. Replace this admission with refusal and producer/doctor no-probe regressions plus removal/restoration evidence; no specification change is needed.


WHAT EACH ONE IS, in one line, so the fix is the rule and not the instance. R1 and R3 are the pnpm reader admitting a shape YAML would not: apply YAML's own separator and lookahead rules at the point of admission, before any scalar is read, and refuse by named reason. R2 is the resolver exporting the canonicalised target where native runs the invocation as given: probe what native would probe, never the canonical form. R4 is env admitted with no program argument: an env invocation without a non-blank program is a refusal, and the test at composite/tests.rs:4719 that expects admission is wrong and must flip.

PROVE EACH BY REMOVAL — break the line, name the failing test and assertion, restore — and assert reasons, never is_err(). Fresh built-doctor reproductions exist for every one of the four; each fix must turn its reproduction into a named refusal with no execution marker.

GATES, crate-scoped and sequential, never a boxed workspace run: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; every crate suite green; the exact coverage steps on the committed bytes, stating the three numbers (the box cannot execute the boundary tests — say so, and the controller takes the capable-host number); openspec validate --all --strict. Notes describe; they never instruct a gate — two chiefs have rejected "return this to the smith" from panel prose.

DO NOT TICK 8.8. Parts (a)–(c) only; (d), 8.10, 9.6, 10.6–10.8, 11.1–11.4, groups 14–15 are not yours. Frozen contracts, policy/phase-machine.json, fixtures/, reference/, extensions/dsh/, docs/decisions/ do not move; 0056 stays proposed. Record what you delivered and what remains.

provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, `policy/schemas/`, and `reference/` are read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

members.adversarial:
Read-only adversarial review of every commit in 81d7fe87..461429025f88523d055395f890b5ae0a4f79a9eb, within R1-R4. No fixes or commits. Two concrete MEDIUM residuals; no unresolved high/critical finding.

A1 — MEDIUM, security, R3 lookahead is not enforced at the package-heading admission path. The new guard at crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters/composite.rs:981 only runs through pnpm_ignored_line. The indent-2 packages path at :1524-1530 strips pre-colon padding and reads the scalar without that guard. Reproduction: in the complete install used by the built-doctor tests, use the lock `lockfileVersion: '9.0'\npackages:\n  debug@2.6.9` + 1014 ASCII spaces + `:\n    resolution: {integrity: sha512-D}\n`. The raw implicit block-key span is 1025 characters (11 key characters + 1014 spaces). PyYAML 6.0.2 rejects it with ScannerError, 'mapping values are not allowed here', consistent with YAML 1.2.2 section 8.2.2 and productions 193/154 (https://yaml.org/spec/1.2.2/#822-block-mappings). Fresh target/debug/brokkr doctor instead reports successful v22.23.2 availability and composite f742ba0ece3e4684adf8398132b688a2ca70d6397b1f29fcef7e2b3ea15eb80d, and both dsh and node execution markers appear. The control with 1013 spaces (1024-character span) is valid and reports exactly that digest. The original ignored peerDependencies 1025-character case now refuses by the lookahead cause and leaves no markers. Thus the same pre-colon lookahead boundary remains bypassable at another block-key admission point.

A2 — MEDIUM, correctness, R2 adds Linux-specific version-success assertions to Unix tests. crates/brokkr-cli/tests/doctor_dsh_selection.rs:2741-2749 and crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters/composite/tests.rs:2718-2727 run the absolute /usr/bin/env --version and assert success; the CLI test additionally requires a version line and later an ok doctor line. On macOS with Apple's system env, --version is unsupported: the option parser reaches usage(), exits 1 and prints no version. Consequently a_dsh_alias_of_env_is_refused_and_an_admitted_alias_runs_as_selected fails at :2742 and the_selected_invocation_is_not_replaced_by_its_canonical_target fails at :2725, breaking the configured macos-latest cargo-test leg. This is a source-based conclusion, not a claimed native macOS execution: Apple's published source uses getopt with '-0C:iP:S:u:v', no version option, and usage exits 1 (https://github.com/apple-oss-distributions/shell_cmds/blob/main/env/env.c).
